children: The Debt Management Office's sale of 900 million pounds ($1.2 billion) in September 2049 index-linked gilts on Thursday attracted solid demand, with a bid to cover ratio of 3.58 times. The real yield on the index-linked gilt--which offers protection against inflation--stood at 2.496%, with a price of 89.16 pounds. High energy prices helped boost demand for the bonds, even as conventional 10-year and 30-year gilt yields hit multiyear highs this week. "We think the case for owning linkers here outright is much stronger than nominal gilts, given the backdrop of a soft domestic economy and rising energy prices," RBC Capital Markets strategists say in a note. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
